(2) From 2000 to 2024, desertification of the study area experienced a process of expansion, fluctuation, and reversal, with recovery being the dominant trend overall. Specifically, in northern China, the proportion of non-desertification consistently remained above 27%, while Mongolia was dominated by moderate and heavy desertification. (3) The area of severe desertification significantly decreased, and was largely converted to lighter desertification degrees. (4) Precipitation and livestock density emerged as key predictors of desertification patterns, with their relative contributions varying across ecological domains. The XGBoost–SHAP analysis further revealed nonlinear predictive associations and interactions among climatic and socioeconomic variables, highlighting the spatial heterogeneity of factors associated with desertification. The results provided scientific evidence and methodological support for the construction of the China–Mongolia–Russia Economic Corridor and the regional achievement of the land degradation neutrality (LDN) goal.

title: Combinatorial Selection of Multi-Pass ICESat-2 ATL24 Calibration Tracks for Sentinel-2 Satellite-Derived Bathymetry
summary: ICESat-2 ATL24 data provide along-track shallow-water depths that can serve as spaceborne calibration information for satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB). A study area is usually crossed by multiple passes, but the tracks differ in quality, depth coverage, and spatial coverage. Existing studies still mainly pool all tracks, use a single pass, or refine the data point by point, and no systematic method yet exists for selecting among large numbers of candidate-track combinations. We formulate ATL24 track selection as a combinatorial optimization problem whose objective is the bathymetric retrieval error, measured against independent airborne lidar bathymetry (ALB) reference depths within the study area so that selection requires local survey data, and test it in three coral-reef areas whose depth ranges and track-quality structures complement one another, using two retrieval models of different flexibility, XGBoost and the Stumpf band-ratio model. On a 16-track controlled pool small enough to enumerate, with the exhaustive global optimum as ground truth, a genetic algorithm (GA) reproduced the global optimum exactly in three of the six cases formed by the three study areas and two models and came within 1.28% of it in the other three, while evaluating fewer than 1% of all possible subsets; on randomly composed pools the GA approached the optimum equally reliably, whereas random search with the same number of evaluations found it with a probability below 1%. The GA was then extended to full candidate pools of 42–70 tracks, corresponding to 1012–1021 subsets, and compared with four conventional practices under spatial-block five-fold cross-validation. Relative to pooling all tracks, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) fell by 9.2–63.3% for XGBoost and by 2.2–30.5% for Stumpf (a magnitude sensitive to the Stumpf fitting settings), and all of these gains kept their sign under strict spatial isolation, in which the calibration points inside the test blocks were also withheld. The gains were concentrated in the deepest water, and some shallower depth bands deteriorated. These results show that the value of an ATL24 calibration track is determined jointly by track quality, coverage complementarity, and the downstream model, and that, where local reference depths are available, task-oriented combinatorial selection is better suited than the per-track thresholds and rankings tested here to the quality control of multi-pass calibration data.

title: Subpixel Low-Intensity Fire Detection in Wide-Swath Remote Sensing: Dual-Scale Thermal Background Adaptation and Spatiotemporal Semantic Constraints
summary: Subpixel low-intensity fires are difficult to detect in wide-swath imagery because mixed pixels weaken their thermal signals, whereas industrial facilities and photovoltaic panels can generate false alarms. We propose a dual-scale adaptive thermal background thresholding method based on spatiotemporal semantic constraints and conduct experiments using the detection of crop straw burning in China as a specific application scenario. The method combines scene-wide thermal state classification with local neighborhood statistics to adjust the above-background threshold and recover additional weak fire candidates. Farmland support, a persistent heat source prior derived from long-term VIIRS observations, and candidate-to-source proximity are then applied to newly added candidates to suppress non-target anomalies while preserving strong thermal detections. Experiments using 36 Wide Swath Imager scenes, near-contemporaneous Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite observations, field surveys in Anhui Province, and 260 Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer scenes support the method’s use for weak fire candidate screening under heterogeneous thermal backgrounds. Targeted field surveys found fresh crop residue burn marks at 10 of 12 selected T0 candidate sites (83.3%). This proportion applies only to the surveyed candidate set and does not represent an estimate of overall detection accuracy. In the MODIS transfer experiment, detections near industrial facilities decreased from 45.17% for the official products to 7.92% with the transferred method. The proposed framework supports the regional screening of low-intensity fire candidates and targeted field verification, with persistent heat source information providing contextual constraints.

title: HSFFNet: A Height-Guided Spatial–Frequency Fusion Network for Crown-Level Tree Species Segmentation
summary: High-resolution UAV RGB imagery and canopy height models (CHMs) can provide complementary appearance and structural information for tree crown analysis. However, existing multimodal segmentation methods often treat optical and height data as parallel feature sources, and the structural role of canopy height in tree crown representation remains insufficiently explored. To address this limitation, we propose HSFFNet, a Height-Guided Spatial–Frequency Fusion Network for crown-level tree species segmentation, which exploits CHM-derived structural information to enhance RGB representations across multiple feature scales and frequency components. Specifically, a Scale-Aligned Height Encoder (SAHE) is introduced to construct hierarchical height representations corresponding to the multilevel RGB features. A Height-Guided Spatial–Frequency Fusion (HGSFF) module then models appearance and structure interaction in the spatial domain while using canopy height to regulate frequency-specific RGB responses. Finally, a Multi-Scale Height-Frequency Refinement (MHFR) module is applied to extract localized height variations at multiple spatial ranges to complement structural details. Experiments on two tree species datasets show that HSFFNet achieves mIoU values of 78.26% and 79.05%, respectively, outperforming several representative RGB-based and multimodal segmentation methods.

title: Orientation-Aware Feature Flow Network for Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
summary: Remote sensing oriented object detection faces the challenge of maintaining consistent rotational geometric information throughout feature representation, cross-scale propagation, and bounding-box localization. To address this issue, this paper proposes a direction–scale collaborative optimization method for oriented object detection. A frozen DINOv3 encoder is adopted as the semantic feature source to enhance target discrimination in complex backgrounds through global semantic modeling and dense feature representation. Rotation-Oriented Space-to-Depth Convolution (ROSPD) is introduced to preserve fine-grained spatial structures and local directional-response cues during downsampling. In addition, a Rotation-Aware Residual Fusion (RARF) module estimates local axial agreement between adjacent feature levels and uses it to condition residual multi-scale fusion. A ProbIoU–NWD joint loss with deterministic target-size-adaptive weighting is further constructed: it emphasizes NWD supervision for small objects and gradually returns to ProbIoU as target size increases, thereby improving localization stability under low-overlap conditions. Experiments on DIOR-R and DOTA-v1.5 demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves the detection and localization performance of multi-scale oriented objects in complex remote sensing scenes.

title: Reconstruction of VIIRS 375 m Resolution Data for Algal Bloom Detection
summary: The Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) is fundamentally constrained by a 750 m spatial resolution in its multispectral channels, limiting its capacity for algal bloom observations. This study proposed a Spatial Residual Correlation Method (SRCM) to reconstruct 375 m VIIRS ocean color products using the 375 m I1 band (638 nm). This method is based on the scale-invariance assumption that the linear relationships (k(λ)) between spatial residuals between M-bands and I1 band are almost identical at 375 m and 750 m, and calculates a scene-specific k(λ) to derive 375 m spatial residuals of M-bands from those of the I1 band. The reconstructed 375 m remote sensing reflectance (Rrs) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) images show additional spatial variation compared with the native 750 m products. The ratios of reconstructed to native products are 1.001 ± 0.029 for Rrs(443) and 0.997 ± 0.032 for Chl-a, indicating consistency with the native 750 m products. The 375 m ratio of algal bloom (RAB) maps show finer spatial patterns for reported algal bloom events in the tested coastal waters. These results suggest that SRCM may be useful for algal bloom detection in the tested coastal waters, while further comparisons with independent imagery at higher spatial resolution would allow the accuracy of the added features to be assessed.

title: A Spectral–Spatial Fusion Network for Hyperspectral Small Water Body Extraction
summary: In hyperspectral imagery, small water bodies are often difficult to delineate due to their limited spatial extent, irregular shapes, and spectral similarity to surrounding land-cover types, which can lead to missed detections and fragmented boundaries. To address these challenges, this study proposes a spectral–spatial fusion network with parallel 3D CNN and ResNet-50 branches to extract complementary spectral–spatial and hierarchical spatial features. A progressive gated spectral–spatial fusion (PGSSF) module integrates these features across successive scales to help preserve weak water-body features and reduce background interference. The fused features are further processed by a scale-adaptive local–global (SALG) module, which combines local spatial details with broader contextual information to better characterize narrow watercourses and their continuity. Experiments were conducted using hyperspectral imagery from the Dongting Lake region, with comparisons against the normalized difference water index (NDWI), U-Net, Swin Transformer, and WaterFormer. The proposed method achieved a Water IoU of 80.68%, a recall of 90.33%, and an F1-score of 89.31%, with Water IoU exceeding that of WaterFormer by 4.76 percentage points. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed method for regional small-water-body mapping and surface-water monitoring.

title: DecoupledFM: Decoupling Invariant and Specific Representations for Robust Cross-Modal Feature Matching
summary: Cross-modal image matching, such as between optical-SAR or RGB-infrared images, remains a critical yet challenging task due to severe, non-linear radiometric distortions that plague existing end-to-end matchers. We identify feature entanglement as a potential cause of this performance degradation: standard backbones implicitly couple modality-invariant geometric structures with modality-specific appearances. This coupling, while effective within a single domain, breaks down under drastic domain shifts, leading to matching failure. To address this, we propose DecoupledFM, a semi-dense matching framework that uses separate invariant and specific feature branches. The core of our method is the Invariance-Guided Disentanglement Module (IGDM), which enforces a trio of synergistic constraints—feature cyclic substitution for modality invariance, reconstruction with an orthogonality loss for disentanglement completeness, and keypoint score prediction for geometric saliency awareness—to achieve a principled decomposition. This novel design effectively injects the structural priors of sparse descriptors into a high-precision semi-dense architecture. During inference, only the disentangled invariant features are used for robust coarse matching via an Efficient Cross-View Matching Module, while fine refinement also uses backbone features. Extensive experiments on 20 challenging subsets demonstrate that DecoupledFM achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing methods.

title: Quality-Gated Integration of Predicted Fields for Maize–Soybean Mapping with AlphaEarth Foundations
summary: Timely field-level crop mapping remains difficult where current labels and reliable parcel boundaries are scarce. This study examined whether 2024 AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) annual embeddings could support maize–soybean mapping through unsupervised clustering followed by label-assisted semantic assignment and whether Fields of the World (FTW) predictions could convert pixel clusters into reliable parcel-level maps. The 64-dimensional AEF features at 10 m resolution were clustered without crop labels in an agricultural region of northern Northeast China. After the cluster solution was fixed, the field observations were used for semantic assignment and spatially blocked assessment. At the 652 route-based reference points collected in this study, direct AEF clustering yielded F1-scores of 0.944 for maize and 0.942 for soybean, with a macro-F1 of 0.943 for binary maize–soybean retrieval. Unconditional parcel assignment increased spatial regularity but reduced agreement with the reference observations. A quality gate based on pixel support, within-field purity, and under-segmentation risk retained a macro-F1 of 0.936 while reducing small patches by 31.0%. Selective use of predicted fields reduced fragmentation while preserving most of the sample-based accuracy of direct AEF clustering, offering a way to control the loss of pixel-level crop information during parcel aggregation.

title: From Pixels to Piezometers: Bridging Satellite Gravimetry and Groundwater-Level Analysis to Estimate Aquifer Specific Yield
summary: Groundwater is a critical resource in arid and semi-arid environments, where it supports agriculture and ensures drinking water. However, in many regions, including Morocco, this resource is experiencing significant stress, urging the need to understand the aquifers’ behavior. In this context, providing estimates of specific yield (Sy) is essential. This study combines terrestrial water storage (TWS) from GRACE-SeDA (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Self-Supervised Data Assimilation), and the groundwater storage (GWS) residual obtained from it by subtracting modeled soil moisture, snow water equivalent, and reservoir storage, with groundwater levels. A detailed analysis of groundwater-level time series using Sen’s slope shows a general and systematic depletion in almost all of the piezometers, with level decline ranging from weak trends to strong declines above −0.14 m/month. Similarly, the cumulative monthly GWS from the median of the 25-member ensemble shows a decreasing trend with a Sen’s slope of −13.23 million cubic meters (MCM) per month. A robust Huber loss function is employed to optimize Sy by minimizing the residuals between derived GWS anomalies and changes inferred from groundwater-level observations. Sy estimates exhibit spatial variability across the aquifer, ranging from 0.59 to 3.49% for GWS-derived values. The specific yield estimates are drawn from a 15-member ensemble crossing three soil moisture and five snow water equivalent sources. The obtained results fall within the range of observed Sy values. Nevertheless, uncertainties in remote sensing retrievals, spatial resolution, and subsurface heterogeneity limit the robustness of the approach.

title: Joint Assimilation of FY-3E Microwave Sounding and Ground-Based Microwave Radiometer Observations Incorporating AI-Based Cloudy-Sky Profile Retrievals over Complex Terrain on the Eastern Margin of the Tibetan Plateau
summary: Forecasting convective precipitation over complex terrain requires accurate thermodynamic initialization. We developed a WRFDA 3D-Var framework combining nominally clear-sky FY-3E MWTS-3/MWHS-2 radiances, artificial-neural-network (ANN)-retrieved cloudy-sky thermodynamic profiles, and ground-based microwave radiometer (MWR) profiles. In a 5–15 July 2024 inner-domain sample, cloud routing assigned 66.1% of MWTS-3 and 66.9% of MWHS-2 fields of view to the cloudy-sky pathway. Independent radiosonde validation yielded RMSEs of 2.537 K for land temperature and 1.071 g kg−1 for bias-corrected land specific humidity, although a −1.748 K cold bias remained in temperature. Principal precipitation comparisons of four experiments (CTRL, FY, MWR, and FY-MWR) used a common CV7 background-error covariance configuration across nine daily forecasts over Chongqing during 7–15 July. During the principal 10–11 July event, MWR performed comparatively well at selected light-to-moderate precipitation thresholds, whereas FY-MWR had the highest TS at the highest 24 h thresholds. In pooled nine-day verification, CTRL retained the highest threat scores at 0.1–50 mm, while FY-MWR had the highest point estimate at 100 mm (0.083 versus 0.048 for CTRL); however, the paired bootstrap confidence interval for the FY-MWR-minus-CTRL difference included zero. Instability, convective inhibition, moisture-flux convergence, and vertical-motion diagnostics showed time-dependent relationships with precipitation differences. The results therefore indicate event- and intensity-dependent forecast responses rather than uniformly improved forecasts.

title: Climatic Controls of Interannual Variability in Forest Land Surface Phenology Across Poland
summary: Understanding how consistently forest phenology responds from year to year is important for characterizing vegetation responses to climatic variability, yet most studies have focused on long-term phenological trends. Here, we assessed the spatial patterns and environmental controls of detrended interannual variability in the start (SOS) and end (EOS) of the growing season across Polish forests during 2003–2025. SOS and EOS were derived from MODIS NDVI time series, while climatic controls were evaluated using variable-specific preseason windows. Generalized additive models were used to relate phenological variability to long-term climatic conditions, interannual climate variability, aridity, and topography. SOS and EOS variability showed distinct spatial patterns and contrasting climatic sensitivities. SOS was most strongly associated with temperature during the 30-day preseason, whereas EOS showed weaker and more variable climatic relationships. The relevant preseason periods differed among climatic variables and between SOS and EOS. Environmental relationships were predominantly nonlinear, with important effects of temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, solar radiation, aridity, and elevation. The models explained 35.2% and 51.6% of the deviance in SOS and EOS variability, respectively. These findings demonstrate that interannual variability provides complementary information to long-term phenological trends and that SOS and EOS respond differently to climatic and environmental conditions.

title: Exploring Drivers of Structural Variability in Norway Spruce Stands Using Airborne LiDAR
summary: Airborne LiDAR provides a powerful framework for objectively describing forest structure across multiple spatial scales. From LiDAR points to a unit of area, to descriptors of individual trees, to cohorts of trees, to the stand, or at a landscape level, its analytical value can create a hierarchical understanding of drivers affecting the structural variability of trees and their spatial organisation on multiple levels. In this study, we analysed the structure of relatively pure Norway spruce (Picea abies (L.) Karst.) stands in the Ciucaș Mountains (Brașov County, Romania) using airborne LiDAR data. The point cloud was processed in R using an open-source workflow comprising ground classification, terrain modelling, height normalisation, canopy height modelling, treetop detection, and crown delineation. Structural metrics were derived hierarchically, from individual trees to summary statistics for tree cohorts within 500 m2 grid cells, and subsequently to stand-level statistics across grid cells within spruce stands. The geospatial dataset consisted of 58,708 grid cells grouped in 147 stands; for inferential analyses, a filtered dataset of 42,015 cells was retained, covering a total area of 2075.6 hectares. We applied a four-part analytical framework: (i) hierarchical mixed-effects models at the cell level, (ii) quantification of within-stand structural heterogeneity, (iii) stand-level structural typology based on principal component analysis and k-means clustering, and (iv) integration of disturbance history using combined Potapov (pre-2001) and Hansen (2001–2022) forest loss layers. The analysis revealed several patterns consistent with ecological expectations: mean canopy height increased with stand age, slope, and topographic position, whereas it decreased significantly with elevation. Canopy cover increased with elevation, slope, and topographic position, whereas the number of LiDAR-detected trees per cell increased with elevation but decreased with age and slope. The null model intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.252 to 0.408, indicating appreciable between-stand variation alongside a larger within-stand residual component. Structural heterogeneity increased strongly with slope and, to a lesser extent, with northness. The stand typology identified five structural types: low-stature dense uniform, mid-height heterogeneous, tall closed uniform, tall open simplified, and very tall closed complex. Mapped tree cover loss occupied a small fraction of the retained forest sample and was associated with lower mean canopy height (approximately 1 m), lower canopy cover (approximately 4 percentage points), smaller mean crown area (approximately 2 m2), and a slightly lower number of LiDAR-detected trees per cell. These associations do not identify the causes of disturbance or its overall historical importance. In the Ciucaș Mountains, LiDAR-derived metrics provide a spatially explicit baseline for characterising spruce stand structure and its associations with stand age, topography, and mapped disturbance history.

title: Episodic Discharge Is the Dominant Correlate of Turbidity Variability in the Slave River Plume Zone of Great Slave Lake: Evidence from 40 Years of Satellite Observations
summary: Lake surface temperature (LST) and NDTI-based optical turbidity are important indicators of water quality and ecosystem dynamics in northern lakes, where climate warming and river discharge strongly influence thermal structure and sediment transport. This study used multi-sensor satellite observations processed in Google Earth Engine to examine long-term (1984–2024) variability in LST and NDTI-based optical turbidity within the Slave River–Great Slave Lake system, Northwest Territories, Canada, using Landsat, MODIS-Aqua and Sentinel-2 imagery. Landsat (1984–2024) and MODIS Aqua (2002–2024) indicated open-water warming of approximately +0.06 and +0.07 °C yr−1, respectively; only the Landsat trend was statistically significant (p = 0.038 versus p = 0.073). The Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI), used as a relative optical proxy for turbidity, exhibited strong interannual variability that co-varied primarily with Slave River discharge (MODIS Aqua r = 0.91, n = 23, t = 9.80; Landsat 1984–2024 r = 0.72, n = 41, t = 6.41; both p < 0.0001). Principal Component Analysis revealed discharge and NDTI-based optical turbidity as the dominant modes of variability, explaining 65% of the total variance, while LST loaded mainly on a separate component, accounting for a further 32%. The 2020 high-flow event produced the most extensive NDTI-based optical turbidity episode within the 40-year study period, with elevated NDTI consistently detected across all satellite platforms, followed by a marked decline through 2024. Monthly analysis revealed a discharge-dependent NDTI-based optical turbidity lag, with peak NDTI-based optical turbidity occurring concurrently with or within one month of peak discharge during high-flow years but delayed by up to 3–4 months during low-flow years. Spatial analyses further demonstrated persistent NDTI-based optical turbidity intensification near the Slave River mouth and the southwestern basin. These findings indicate that although LST shows a positive but sensor-dependent warming tendency, NDTI variability within the Slave River Plume Zone (SRPZ) was primarily associated with episodic high-discharge conditions consistent with sediment transport processes dominating optical water quality. The study further highlights the value of multi-sensor satellite observations for long-term environmental monitoring in remote subarctic lake systems.

title: Inventory-Constrained Monthly Mapping of China’s Sectoral CO2 Emissions at 1 Km Using Earth Observation and Emission-Source Data
summary: Kilometer-scale, sector-specific CO2 inventories support atmospheric modeling and regional mitigation. We developed an inventory-constrained monthly 1 km CO2 allocation product for China covering 2000–2024 and six sectors. Prescribed Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research (EDGAR) sector-month totals were conserved and spatially redistributed using sector-specific combinations of settlement, infrastructure, and emission-source data; the product therefore does not independently estimate aggregate emissions. Combined emissions increased from 3612.7 Mt CO2 in 2000 to 12,034.1 Mt CO2 in 2024, an increase of 233.1%. Evaluation against separate EDGAR gridmaps for 2024 assessed cell-magnitude agreement, spatial ranking, and top-10% hotspot overlap, but was only partially independent because of the shared EDGAR lineage. Buildings showed the strongest agreement within the residential benchmark scope (r = 0.906, ρ = 0.831; overlap = 70.6%), whereas power achieved only 12.0% positive-union overlap. Evaluations of transport and the industrial sectors were limited by benchmark compatibility. Comparison with the Global Emission Modeling System (GEMS) showed strong common-scope rank agreement (ρ = 0.834 in 2012 and 0.823 in 2021). The framework can be adapted to regions with compatible emission totals and spatial predictors, subject to region-specific evaluation.

title: Martian Mesospheric Gravity-Wave-Related Perturbations During Dust Storms Revealed by ACS-TGO Observations
summary: Gravity waves (GWs) are important for understanding the coupling between dust activity and atmospheric dynamics on Mars. Using temperature and water-vapor profiles from the Near-Infrared channel of the Atmospheric Chemistry Suite (ACS-NIR) onboard the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO), we investigate wave-related temperature perturbations during global and regional dust-storm periods. Comparisons between Mars Years (MY) 34 and 35 reveal a localized enhancement of wave-related perturbations at southern high latitudes, particularly between 60°S and 90°S and 40–90 km. This enhancement persists after controlling for differences in observational sampling. The gravity-wave-related potential-energy proxy is approximately 2–3 times larger during the MY34 global dust storm, with a weaker enhancement during the regional event. These variations coincide with substantial differences in background temperature, static stability, and zonal winds, suggesting that dust-related changes in the atmospheric environment may modify wave propagation and filtering. Water-vapor abundance is also higher in the same region, but is more likely associated with dust-driven large-scale circulation, while wave-related processes may provide additional local modulation. These results provide observational constraints on dust–wave–water coupling in the Martian middle atmosphere.

title: Spatiotemporal Evolution of Mining-Induced Surface Subsidence in Thick Unconsolidated-Layer Coal–Cropland Overlapping Areas Using Multi-Temporal UAV LiDAR and Leveling Measurements
summary: Mining-induced subsidence affects cropland use and land management in coal–cropland overlapping areas. Leveling provides high-precision subsidence time series but limited spatial sampling, whereas multi-temporal unmanned aerial vehicle light detection and ranging (UAV LiDAR) provides spatially continuous terrain-change information, although the uncertainty of digital elevation model (DEM) differencing must be assessed. Three UAV LiDAR surveys (30 May 2025, 25 December 2025, and 14 June 2026) and leveling measurements (March 2025–April 2026) were combined to analyze subsidence at the 32311 working face of Xutuan Coal Mine, Anhui Province, China, during working-face advance and after mining cessation. The level of detection at the 95% confidence level (LoD95) was calculated from elevation residuals in stable areas, and LiDAR-derived subsidence was validated against leveling measurements at 12 points. The LoD95 values of the two cross-sensor differencing periods were 131.9 and 148.8 mm, indicating that changes smaller than approximately 0.13–0.15 m could not be reliably distinguished from measurement error in this study. Leveling-derived cumulative subsidence at these points ranged from 19.76 to 392.95 mm during 30 May–19 December 2025, comprising 19.76–69.75 mm at the six weak-subsidence points and 185.13–392.95 mm at the six strong-subsidence points. LiDAR-derived subsidence showed a strong relationship with leveling measurements at the six strong-subsidence points (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 29.9 mm), whereas the relationship was weak at the six weak-subsidence points (R2 = 0.15). At seven representative leveling points, post-cessation residual subsidence accounted for 15.9–31.2% (mean 20.8%) of the final cumulative subsidence recorded during the leveling period. Relative to 30 May 2025, the area with subsidence exceeding 150 mm increased from 15.31 ha on 25 December 2025 to 16.73 ha on 14 June 2026. The two techniques thus provide complementary temporal and spatial information: leveling measurements reveal the persistence of post-cessation subsidence, while UAV LiDAR characterizes changes in the spatial distribution of cumulative subsidence. Continued monitoring after mining cessation is therefore necessary to capture ongoing surface movement and its spatial characteristics.

title: Improving Hail Diagnosis in Thunderstorms by Combining Radar and Lightning Detection Data
summary: Recent studies indicate an increasing frequency of hailstorms in the Mediterranean region, strengthening the need for improved monitoring and detection methods due to their impacts on human safety and socio-economic activities. This study proposes a real-time method for hail diagnosis in thunderstorms based on the joint use of X-band weather radars and lightning measurements. The approach integrates the Vertically Integrated Liquid Density (VILD) algorithm with a new version of the lightning jump algorithm (hail lightning jump), relating hail growth mechanisms to VILD maxima and lightning-derived variables. Hail reports were used to classify hailstorm severity and link hail occurrence with radar and lightning variables. The 31 confirmed hailstorms examined in Southern Italy show comparable sensitivity of the radar- and lightning-based methods, which identify 80.6% and 77.4% of the events, respectively. When combined using a logical “OR” configuration, the fraction of identified hail events increases to 93.5%. Lightning-based analysis over the Italian Peninsula shows higher lightning activity for very large hail events (≥5 cm) than for large hail cases (2–5 cm). A strong positive correlation between maximum hail size and lightning activity was also found. These results highlight the benefits of a combined approach and the crucial role of lightning activity in diagnosing hail formation and size in thunderstorms.

title: Contrasting Water-Partitioning Responses to Land-Use Change and Climate Perturbations in a Forested Mountain Catchment
summary: Forested mountain catchments play a critical role in regulating regional water resources, yet the effects of land-use change and precipitation–temperature perturbations on internal water partitioning and its seasonal and spatial variability remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we integrated remotely sensed land-cover information and MODIS-derived normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) with a calibrated and validated Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) model to examine hydrological sensitivities and non-additive responses under three land-use configurations and controlled climate perturbations in the upper Pi River Basin, China. Land-cover transitions affected only 2.7% of the study area and produced relatively small hydrological differences among land-use configurations, whereas a 20% precipitation increase enhanced soil-profile percolation (PERC) and surface runoff (SURQ) by 28.62% and 49.81%, respectively; 2 °C warming increased actual evapotranspiration (ET) by 3.58% but reduced SURQ by 5.39%. Under the combined scenario of 20% higher precipitation and 2 °C warming, ET and SURQ increased by 7.15% and 42.06%, respectively, with a non-additive SURQ deviation of −2.36 percentage points; ET sensitivity to precipitation peaked in August, coinciding with the NDVI maximum, whereas sensitivity to warming peaked in May, and soil water storage (SW) responses to warming differed in direction among subbasins. These findings reveal contrasting influences of precipitation supply and temperature-related evaporative demand on hydrological pathways, with component-specific non-additive effects and distinct seasonal and spatial responses. These patterns support the use of remotely sensed vegetation information and distributed hydrological modeling to identify climate-sensitive periods and evaluate spatial differences in water availability in forested mountain catchments.

title: Common Spatial Support and Registration Networks for Reproducible ArcticDEM Elevation Change Analysis
summary: Comparisons of elevation change from repeat digital elevation models (DEMs) depend on which pixels are evaluated and which DEM pairs are used for alignment. These effects were examined using ArcticDEM strips, four terrain windows with known perturbations, and four acquisitions at the Batagay megaslump. In the original single-realization tests, the maximum joint-gradient component and protected-change median errors were 0.087 and 0.027 m. In 480 additional paired perturbations, all joint-gradient estimates met the prescribed 0.50 m component tolerance; the median maximum component error was 0.026 m. On the observed Batagay terrain, joint-gradient, xDEM Nuth–Kääb, and historical internal Nuth–Kääb fits were accepted for 16, 17, and 14 of 18 pair-by-reference combinations, respectively, under matched candidate sampling. In the historical two-implementation comparison, restricting the combined-reference network to shared edges increased the July–September 2024 root-mean-square difference between the two change maps from 1.755 to 2.577 m on 184,120 identical target cells. Changing from pair-specific to fixed evaluation support had little effect on that interval. These results distinguish sensitivity to graph selection from sensitivity to the terrain evaluated. Independent elevations were unavailable at Batagay, so the outputs cannot be ranked by field accuracy.

title: Measurand-Aware Inter-Platform Consistency Assessment of GOES Land Surface Temperature Harmonization
summary: Cross-platform land surface temperature (LST) harmonization is often evaluated by agreement of individual observations, although urban analyses commonly rely on spatial differences and temporal changes. We investigated whether improving agreement in urban-core and surrounding-ring LST also improves their core–ring contrast and pre-to-post-sunset transition. Using Advanced Baseline Imager observations from Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES)-16, -17, -18, and -19 over western North American cities during 2019–2026, we evaluated five cohorts using established mean-squared-error (MSE) decomposition and cross-validated model selection at each measurand. Component root-mean-squared error (RMSE) decreased by 29.3–59.7%, whereas core–ring contrast RMSE ranged from an 11.5% reduction to a 13.1% increase. Loss of residual covariance offset 94.6–114.0% of gross variance-plus-bias gains. In the post hoc 2026 temporal evaluation of the same 75 cities used for 2025 calibration, core and ring RMSE declined by 59.7% and 56.1%, but contrast RMSE reduction was −0.14% (95% crossed city–interval bootstrap interval, −6.75% to +6.48%, with cities and intervals resampled independently). The historical 2021 evaluation likewise showed only a small, uncertain contrast improvement (2.9%; 95% interval, −4.3% to +9.8%). Calibration-based selection retained raw contrasts and transitions, while a residual interval rule withheld uncertain transition direction claims. Independent three-station radiometric comparisons assessed raw satellite products at station scale rather than the complete urban workflow. These findings demonstrate why harmonization performance should be evaluated at the derived scientific quantity, with processing decisions based on its observed cross-platform consistency.

title: Enhanced Chlorophyll Responses to the Interaction Between an Anticyclonic Eddy and Internal Solitary Waves: A Case Study
summary: Mesoscale eddies and internal solitary waves (ISWs) influence upper-ocean chlorophyll variability, yet their roles in the spatial variations in chlorophyll during their interaction remain poorly revealed. Using satellite ocean-color and sunglint imagery, we observed different chlorophyll variabilities in three cases: an ISW-only case, an eddy-only case, and an eddy–ISW interaction case. In the ISW-only case, chlorophyll exhibited coherent, banded, and phase-dependent anomalies, characterized by reduced concentrations near the wave trough but enhanced ones in the trailing region, with a chlorophyll anomaly reaching approximately 0.02 mg m−3. In the eddy-only case, chlorophyll exhibited a distinct low-core but high-periphery structure, with elevated filamentary features concentrated around the eddy boundary and spatially consistent with enhanced finite-size Lyapunov exponent (FSLE). During the eddy–ISW interaction, the ISW crests became strongly deformed near the eddy periphery, consistent with modulation by the mesoscale eddy. Within the eddy interior, the ISW-related banded chlorophyll structure remained evident, whereas near the eddy periphery these bands became curved and spatially overlapped with filamentary chlorophyll structures. The difference in chlorophyll between the eddy–ISW and eddy-only cases increased toward the eddy periphery, reaching approximately 50% at ~1.2R. These observations reveal a multiscale spatial modulation of chlorophyll variability, in which the mesoscale eddy establishes a broader spatial pattern, while ISWs induce propagating fine-scale perturbations. The eddy–ISW interaction primarily regulates and enhances chlorophyll variability near the eddy periphery, rather than producing a uniform response throughout the eddy.

title: PMA-SAM2: Prior-Memory Adapted Framework for Automatic Remote Sensing Water Body Extraction
summary: SAM2 has great potential for remote sensing water body extraction due to its strong feature representation capability. However, when directly applied to the water body segmentation task, SAM2 still faces several challenges, including domain discrepancy, spectral confusion between water bodies and shadow-like objects, significant intra-class variations, and dependence on manual prompts. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the PMA-SAM2, which integrates domain prior injection, prototype memory calibration, and automatic prompt guidance for robust water body extraction. First, a Multi-level Prior Adaptation Module is designed to inject spatial geometric information and texture features into the SAM2 encoder, enabling effective alignment between general visual representations and remote sensing domain features. Then, a Prototype Memory Calibration Module is introduced to dynamically accumulate water feature prototypes under different geographical environments and imaging conditions, improving the model’s robustness to intra-class variations and inter-class spectral ambiguity. Furthermore, an Automatic Prompt Decoder is proposed to transform prototype-retrieved similarity maps into dense prompts, replacing manual prompts and enabling fully automatic water body segmentation. Experimental results on four datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior water body extraction accuracy compared with mainstream segmentation methods, verifying its strong generalization capability and scene adaptability.

title: Source Characteristics of the 2025 Mw 6.0 Aheqi Earthquake: Possible Relationship to the 2024 Mw 7.0 Wushi Earthquake
summary: The 4 December 2025 Mw 6.0 Aheqi earthquake occurred on the Maidan–Shayilamusi Fault system in the western southern Tian Shan, approximately 23 months after the 2024 Mw 7.0 Wushi earthquake. We used ascending- and descending-track Sentinel-1A differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (DInSAR) observations to map coseismic line-of-sight (LOS) deformation, jointly invert fault geometry and distributed slip, calculate Coulomb failure stress changes, and evaluate sequence association using earthquake-catalog statistics and an epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) model. The deformation field is elongated NEE–SWW, with maximum displacement toward the satellite of approximately 6 cm. The preferred model has a strike of 242°, dip of 40°, rake of 77°, and maximum slip of 0.21 m concentrated at depths of 4.89–7.46 km, corresponding to Mw 5.91. The joint inversion yields an RMSE of 0.0145 m. Coulomb stress calculations indicate positive ΔCFS at the Aheqi source within the principal rupture-depth interval of 4.89–7.46 km across all three tested receiver-fault geometries. For the preferred geometry, ΔCFS reaches +6.16 bar at the slip-centroid depth of 6.18 km and is close to zero (+0.29 bar) at 10 km, where its sign varies among the tested geometries. At 15 km, ΔCFS is negative for all three geometries. ETAS stochastic declustering assigns the Aheqi event a total triggered-component probability of 82.6% and a background-component probability of 17.4%. Separate attribution analysis yields a 65.7% probability of belonging to the Wushi mainshock’s descendant sequence and a 0.5% probability of direct triggering by the Wushi mainshock. Together with the spatiotemporal compatibility of the two events, these results support a possible interaction within the segmented Maidan–Shayilamusi Fault system, although they do not establish deterministic causation or uniquely identify the physical triggering pathway. The modeled stress pattern also highlights nearby positively loaded fault segments for continued monitoring.

title: FVE: Fire-Management-Aligned Vision–Language Reasoning for UAV-Based Fire-Event Assessment
summary: Existing unmanned aerial vehicle fire monitoring methods primarily recognize visible smoke or flame cues but cannot reliably determine whether an observed anomaly is an uncontrolled fire requiring intervention. This study reformulates UAV fire monitoring from a conventional visual-recognition problem into an event-level reasoning and decision task. We propose Fire-Verify-Expert (FVE), a compact vision–language model that jointly performs smoke and fire cue confirmation, real-fire verification, event-type attribution, and ordered response-priority assessment. FVE incorporates fire-management logic into multimodal preference alignment through a multidimensional Group Relative Policy Optimization objective. Its reward mechanism constrains determination correctness, event-type consistency, rationale–decision consistency, and reasoning quality, while imposing asymmetric penalties on operationally costly errors, particularly missed real fires and severe underestimation of response priority. To support this task, we establish a UAV-oriented dataset of 600 images spanning varied environmental contexts and viewing perspectives, including real fires and visually similar controlled or currently non-actionable smoke/fire events. The dataset provides structured reasoning annotations and ordered response-priority labels. FVE achieves an accuracy/F1-score of 0.917/0.915 for real-fire verification, with a recall of 1.000 for real fires, and an accuracy/F1-score of 0.833/0.706 for response-priority assessment. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of FVE in aligning multimodal vision–language reasoning with fire-management requirements, providing a feasible approach for automated fire-event verification and response prioritization in frontline UAV fire-monitoring workflows.

title: A multi-sensor framework for comparing and integrating optical, C-band and L-band SAR inundation products in tropical floodplain of Australia
summary: Accurate inundated landscape mapping is essential for understanding hydrological connectivity, wetland dynamics and floodplain processes in tropical environments. However, optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) sensors often produce inconsistent inundation estimates due to differences in sensor physics, wavelength sensitivity, vegetation and cloud penetration, and analytical methods. These challenges are amplified in wet–dry tropical systems, where cloud cover, heterogeneous vegetation and seasonal flooding complicate water detection. This study presents a unified, data-driven framework for comparing inundation products derived from Sentinel-2 optical imagery, Sentinel-1 C-band and PALSAR-2 L-band SAR in a tropical floodplain system in northern Australia. Inundated landscape maps were generated using supervised Random Forest classification and unsupervised multi-Otsu thresholding, followed by multi-sensor fusion analysis. Products were validated using wet- and dry-season field observations. Results showed strong seasonal and sensor-specific differences. Sentinel-2 provided the most balanced representation of dry-season floodplain vegetation and inundation, while Sentinel-1 achieved high wet-season accuracy (>0.95) under cloud-affected conditions. PALSAR-2 improved the detection of inundated vegetation and structurally complex environments, reaching an overall accuracy of 0.97. Multi-sensor fusion generally improved spatial coherence and class delineation, but performance varied across sensor combinations. These findings show that optical, C-band SAR and L-band SAR inundation products are not directly interchangeable in tropical wetlands. The proposed framework supports more robust interpretation, comparison and integration of multi-sensor inundation products for wetland monitoring, hydrological assessment and environmental management in data-limited tropical regions.

title: Fusing a foundation model with spatiotemporal correction for automated long-term tracking of rift propagation from satellite imagery: a case study of the amery ice shelf
summary: Long-term satellite monitoring of rift propagation is essential for assessing Antarctic ice shelf stability and projecting sea-level rise. Currently, long-term tracking of rifts still relies on time-consuming manual interpretation, significantly affecting its feasibility for large-scale rift monitoring. Here, we present a novel framework for automatically tracking rift propagation, which fuses the fine-tuned visual foundation model (Segment Anything Model, SAM) and spatiotemporal correction. The SAM enables automated rift extraction using only a few samples without any manual prompts, while the spatiotemporal correction improves the precision of rift mapping for geometric measurements. We applied this framework to automatically monitor key rifts on the Amery Ice Shelf using 768 Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2 images from 2015 to 2025, achieving an F1 score of 98.6% across 11 independent scenes. Rift length and width measurements were in agreement with manual interpretation, with R2 values of 0.979 and 0.999, respectively. Furthermore, our extended monitoring revealed recent structural changes within the rift system on the Amery Ice Shelf. This study offers a new way for automated rift tracking with the foundation model for the first time, having significant potential for long-term monitoring of pan-Antarctic rifts.

title: An ensemble approach driven by spatial interaction for modelling urban epidemic dynamics
summary: Modelling spatial interactions remains a core issue in geographic information science. Faced with the emerging, non-stationary spread of epidemics, the effects and uncertainties of spatial interactions are amplified. Limited by reliance on a single spatial interaction prior, existing models perform well in specific scenarios but suffer from prediction drift across multi-phase epidemics, thereby hindering real-time and dynamic policy adjustments. To address this limitation, we propose an ensemble approach driven by spatial interaction, built upon a foundational metapopulation model. Using the 2022 Shanghai Omicron outbreak as a case study, we evaluated the proposed ensemble model against 14 mechanistic and machine learning baselines. In multi-phase prediction tasks, the proposed ensemble model achieves the best overall performance with mean ranks of 3.25 for RMSE and 4.00 for R2, surpassing all baselines with mean ranks ranging from 5 to 15. Furthermore, it improves mean predictive accuracy by 29% to 72% compared with the non-ensemble models, while reducing the prediction error interval by 10% to 84%. Finally, we generated model-based projections across multiple counterfactual scenarios to explore responses to changes in intervention timing and intensity.

title: A novel satellite embedding-driven SWOT framework for river discharge estimation: a case study of the Yangtze river
summary: Accurate river discharge estimation is essential for water cycle modeling, water hazards prevention, water ecosystem protection and water resource management. However, conventional ground-based gauging networks are often sparsely distributed and insufficient to capture the complex hydrodynamic characteristics within large and heterogeneous river basins. With the rapid advancement of remote sensing technologies, particularly the launch of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission, new opportunities have emerged for large-scale and continuous river discharge estimation. In this study, we develop and evaluate a SWOT-based river discharge estimation framework for the Yangtze River by integrating SWOT RiverSP hydraulic observations organized on the SWORD river network with Satellite Embedding V1 data in a random forest model to capture both hydrodynamic and geomorphological characteristics. The framework is evaluated using temporally separated training and testing observations from nine gauging stations along the Yangtze River mainstream, with station-specific nonlinear empirical models used for comparison. The main conclusions are as follows: 1) The random forest model substantially improves discharge estimation relative to the empirical formulation, with a maximum NSE gain of 0.4372 and an NRMSE reduction of up to 0.1175; 2) The model demonstrates reliable performance across the nine gauging stations, with all stations achieving NSE ≥ 0.72 and the overall performance reaching NSE = 0.8910 and NRMSE = 0.0664; 3) The spatially explicit discharge estimates show strong agreement with reach-scale results (correlation ≈ 0.9), indicating that water level exerts primary control on discharge, while channel width and geometry significantly modulate discharge responses in morphologically complex reaches. These results demonstrate the potential of combining SWOT hydraulics with satellite foundation embeddings to improve discharge estimation.

title: Neighborhood-aware retrieval of a spatial floe fragmentation index for Arctic sea ice using Sentinel-1 SAR and AMSR2
summary: Arctic sea ice fragmentation involves changes in floe area composition, spatial separation, and geometric complexity, which affect lateral melt rates and ice–ocean heat fluxes. Existing metrics primarily characterize floe size distributions or area fractions, limiting their capacity to resolve variations in the spatial arrangement of floes. We propose a spatial floe fragmentation index (SFFI) that jointly quantifies floe area composition, spatial separation, and geometric complexity. Using 416 Sentinel-1 SAR scenes spanning diverse Arctic regions and ice conditions, we extract floe contours to generate 52,074 SFFI reference labels. For samples with comparable floe area composition, higher SFFI values correspond to greater inter-floe spacing and lower circularity, demonstrating that the index captures spatial and geometric differences not represented by area composition alone. To enable daily Arctic monitoring, we develop a neighborhood-aware retrieval framework integrating AMSR2 radiometry, sea ice concentration (SIC), and neighborhood statistics, and evaluate its performance using random forest, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron models. Under the 2016–2024 SAR-scene split, XGBoost with the complete feature set achieves the best performance, with an R2 of 0.6877, an RMSE of 0.3454, and an MAE of 0.2536. Neighborhood-aware features provide relative R2 gains of 4.6% to 10.0% over the SIC-inclusive baselines. The selected model maintained robust predictive performance on the independent 2025 dataset, supporting its temporal transferability. Using the best-performing model, we generate a daily Arctic SFFI product on a 12.5 km grid for 2016–2025. Results show that SFFI captures a pronounced seasonal cycle, with high-SFFI areas expanding during the melt season and contracting during refreezing, while revealing regional differences among Arctic marginal seas.

title: Multi-temporal analysis of reflectance and vegetation index consistency between Sentinel-2 and UAS imagery over a managed broadleaved forest: implications for monitoring
summary: The comparability between satellite-based and uncrewed aerial system (UAS) imagery is critical for multiscale forest monitoring. It enables the integration of fine-resolution observations into a broader satellite-derived spatial and temporal context. Understanding this comparability supports the strategic use of centimeter-resolution UAS data to address fine-scale ecological questions, to serve as gap-filling observations within satellite-based time series during periods of absent data retrievals, and to link fine-scale canopy structural variation to landscape-level vegetation dynamics observed from space. This study investigated the spectral and vegetation index level consistency between Sentinel-2 and UAS multispectral measurements acquired over a 300 ha managed broadleaved forest in Central Europe. UAS data were collected using a fixed-wing platform equipped with a MicaSense Altum multispectral sensor and temporally matched to Sentinel-2 overpasses over a 6-month period at approximately two-week intervals. Cross-platform agreement was quantified using distribution-based similarity metrics, spatial aggregation of UAS data to Sentinel-2 spatial resolution, intrinsic correlation analysis, and single-date regression modeling. At their native spatial resolutions, UAS observations exhibited systematically higher radiometric variability and stronger distributional asymmetry than Sentinel-2 data, particularly in the red-edge band, consistent with increased sensitivity to fine-scale illumination differences and canopy structural heterogeneity, and partly reflecting radiometric differences between individual UAS flights. Spatial aggregation of UAS data reduced this variability but did not fully remove wavelength-dependent discrepancies, with the highest levels of agreement consistently observed in the green, red, and near-infrared bands. Among the vegetation indices, normalized difference metrics, particularly the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and the Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (GNDVI), showed the strongest and most temporally stable cross-platform consistency across both multitemporal distributions and individual acquisition dates. In contrast, simple ratio-based indices and indices incorporating red-edge wavelengths exhibited systematic distributional shifts and reduced temporal robustness. These distributional shifts are consistent with persistent sensor-level spectral response differences rather than index-specific artifacts. Collectively, these findings indicate that normalized difference indices built from spectrally well-matched bands, which largely remove radiometric differences between UAS flights, provide a robust basis for the joint exploitation of UAS and Sentinel-2 observations, enabling consistent multiscale monitoring of broadleaved forests while retaining the complementary advantages of each observational platform.

title: AHI LAI: a seamless 500 m, 4-day leaf area index dataset of the Asia-Pacific region (2015–2025) generated from geostationary Himawari-8/9 observations
summary: Vegetation plays a critical role in Earth system processes, making the monitoring of vegetation dynamics a fundamental component of global change research. Leaf area index (LAI) acts as a primary indicator for assessing vegetation canopy structure. Optical observations from polar-orbiting satellites often experience data gaps because relatively infrequent observation opportunities can coincide with regional cloud cover. High-frequency measurements from geostationary sensors, including the Himawari-8/9 Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI), increase the probability of capturing valid surface signals during transient cloud-free windows. In this study, a Himawari-MODIS fusion framework integrating polar-orbiting satellite LAI observations with geostationary satellite reflectance data was developed and applied to produce a long-term, spatially seamless and high-temporal-resolution AHI-based LAI dataset for the Asia-Pacific. Biome-specific Random Forest models were trained using filtered MODIS LAI as benchmarks to estimate LAI from AHI data. A modified singular spectrum analysis (mSSA) algorithm with spatiotemporal neighbor selection was implemented to reconstruct missing values. The resulting data were subsequently downscaled utilizing spatial texture patterns derived from MODIS LAI data. This AHI LAI product features a 500 m spatial resolution and a 4-day temporal resolution, spanning from 2015 to 2025. Validation against in situ LAI measurements showed that AHI LAI achieved lower RMSE and MAE than MODIS LAI, with values of 1.781 and 1.423 compared with 2.087 and 1.647 for MODIS LAI, respectively. In cloud-prone regions and complex terrains, the AHI LAI product exhibits smoother temporal profiles and lower data dispersion compared to the MODIS LAI product. Furthermore, the AHI LAI product captures timely vegetation responses to moisture stress during drought events. The AHI LAI product may provide continuous data support for ecological monitoring and vegetation dynamics research in the Asia-Pacific region.

title: Retrieval of vegetation leaf equivalent water thickness from GF-5 hyperspectral imagery via physics-guided transfer learning
summary: Vegetation leaf equivalent water thickness (EWT) is an important indicator of plant water status and is relevant to ecological monitoring and vegetation stress assessment. However, hyperspectral retrieval of leaf EWT remains challenging because canopy structural effects and discrepancies between simulated and measured observations can limit model transferability. To address this issue, we developed a physics-guided transfer-learning framework for EWT retrieval using Gaofen-5 Advanced Hyperspectral Imager (GF-5 AHSI) data. A diverse simulation domain was constructed by coupling PROSPECT-D with the 4SAIL and 4-Scale canopy models to represent both relatively homogeneous and structurally complex vegetation. Complementary PCA-derived and physically interpretable spectral features were selected, and four base learners were integrated using out-of-fold stacking. Models were first pretrained on simulated data and subsequently fine-tuned using in-situ observations. Simulation-only pretraining achieved RMSEs of 0.083 kg/m2 on the held-out measured test set and 0.091 kg/m2 on the independent external test set. After fine-tuning, the corresponding RMSEs decreased to 0.056 and 0.071 kg/m2, respectively. Moreover, on the independent external test set, the fine-tuned ensemble reduced RMSE from 0.101 to 0.071 kg/m2 relative to measured-only modeling, further supporting improved transferability. Regional applications over Saihanba and an area within and adjacent to the Northeast China Tiger and Leopard National Park produced spatially coherent EWT patterns, while ensemble model disagreement varied among regions and vegetation types. These results demonstrate that physics-guided simulation pretraining combined with measured-data fine-tuning provides a practical approach for improving the transferability of hyperspectral leaf-EWT retrieval under heterogeneous vegetation conditions.
